# join

<link-summary>Joins path segments with a single separator between them.</link-summary>

<web-summary>join() — Joins path segments with a single separator between them. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function join(...paths: string[]): string;
```

Empty segments are dropped, doubled separators collapse into one, and the result is normalised afterwards — so a `..` written mid-path is resolved rather than carried along.

This is string work, not filesystem work: nothing is checked for existence.

## Parameters

| Parameter  | Type       | Description           |
| :--------- | :--------- | :-------------------- |
| `...paths` | `string[]` | The segments to join. |

## Returns

`string` — the joined, normalised path.

## Examples

### Joining

```javascript
join("a", "b/c"); // => "a/b/c"
join("a", "", "b"); // => "a/b"
join("/a", "../b"); // => "/b"
```
